questions.question:
**​DIRECTIONS:** In the question below are given few statements followed by few conclusion. You have to take the given statements to be true even if they seem to be at variance with the commonly known facts and then decide which of the given conclusions logically follows from the given statements, disregarding commonly known facts.

**Statements:**

All Roads are flowers.

Some flowers are trees.

Some trees are leaves.

All leaves are big.

**Conclusions:**

I. Some roads are trees.

II. Some flowers are big.

III. No flower is big.

options.text: Only either II or III follows

questions.solution:
From the given statements we draw the following least possible Venn diagram

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/646c30504627284f929aa8c797a025bc0da56bce99a96e04f551bb2fe1337148.png] 

Conclusions:

I. Some roads are trees. → False ( This is possibility not definite)

II. Some flowers are big. → False ( This is possibility not definite)

III. No flower is big. → False ( This is possibility not definite)

Here, Conclusion II and III forms a complementary pair.

So, either II or III follow.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] __Important Points__Complementary pair:

1) When both the elements of conclusions are the same.

2) When both the conclusions are false (possible but not definite) individually.

There are two different types of complementary pairs

​1) All - Some not

2) No - Some

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] __Additional Information__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4cdc7830485868658ae2aedfef6893df41106c81ab809676e386d047ba8161f2.png]

questions.question: If X ≥ Y = P > Q ≤ R > Z, which of the following can be concluded?
questions.solution:
**Given statement:** X ≥ Y = P > Q ≤ R > Z

Conclusions:

Option 1) Q ≥ X ≤ Y → Does not follow (As __**X ≥ Y = P > Q**__ ≤ R > Z. So, it can be concluded as 'Q therefore it is false)

Option 2) Z Does not follow (As X ≥ Y = P > __**Q ≤ R > Z**__. Here no relation can be determined between Z and R, therefore it is false)

Option 3) R ≥ Q ≥ P → Does not follow (As X ≥ Y = __**P > Q ≤ R**__ > Z. Here no relation can be determined between P and R, therefore it is false)

Option 4) P ≤ X > Q → Follow (As __**X ≥ Y = P > Q**__ ≤ R > Z. Here, both relations, 'X ≥ P' and 'X > Q' can be determined, therefore is true)

Thus, out of all the options, only 'P ≤ X > Q' can be concluded from the given statement.

Hence, the correct answer is "Option 4".

questions.question:
Two statements are followed by two conclusions numbered I and II. You have to consider these statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts. Decide which of the given conclusions logically follow/s from the given statements.

**Statement**

1. skilling is a necessity for the performance on the jobs.

2. National Education Policy (NEP) is introduced to skill, reskill and upskill people

**Conclusions**

I. Unskilled people can also get the job.

II. NEP will skill the manpower.

options.text: Either conclusion I or II follows.
Neither conclusion I nor II follows.

questions.solution:
Given the statements above:

__**Conclusion I:**__ Unskilled people can also g
et the job.

This conclusion does not logically follow. The first statement says that skilling is a necessity for performance on jobs. It implies that without skill, one would not be able to perform adequately on jobs, thus suggesting that being unskilled may be a barrier to getting a job.

**Conclusion I does not follows.**

__**Conclusion II:**__ NEP will skill the manpower.

This conclusion logically follows from the given statements. According to the second statement, the National Education Policy is introduced to skill, reskill, and upskill people, which implies that it is designed to add skills to the workforce or manpower.

**Conclusion II follows.**

Hence, the correct answer is **"Only conclusion II follows".**

questions.question:
Directions: In the following question below are given a question and two statements numbered I and II. You have to decide whether the data provided in the statements are sufficient to answer the question. Read both the statements and give your answer.

What is the code for 'walks' in the code language?

Statements:

I. In the code language, 'she walks fast' is written as 'he ka to'.

II. In the code language, 'she learns fast' is written as 'jo ka he'.

options.text: If the data in Statement I alone are sufficient to answer the question, while the data in Statement II alone are not sufficient to answer the question.
If the data in Statement II alone are sufficient to answer the question, while the data in Statement I alone are not sufficient to answer the question.
If the data in both the Statements I and II together are necessary to answer the question.
If the data in both the Statements I and II are not sufficient to answer the question.

questions.solution:
**Using statement I:**

I. In the code language, 'she walks fast' is written as 'he ka to'.

We can not determine the code for "walks".

**Using statement II:**

II. In the code language, 'she learns fast' is written as 'jo ka he'.

Using this statement we can not determine the code for "walks".

By combining statements I and II:

I. In the code language, 'she walks fast' is written as 'he ka to'.

II. In the code language, 'she learns fast' is written as 'jo ka he'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3c6e6dee30ac9ec88726607b31868be1961a613c9ddb7f05bc79a9aa83cc3805.png] 

The words 'she' and 'fast' are common in both sentences and so are the codes 'he' and 'ka'. Implies, 'he' and 'ka' are the codes for 'she' and 'fast' but not necessarily in the same order.

It further implies that 'to' is the code for the word 'walks' and both statements are required to answer the question.

Hence, **"data in both statements I and II together are necessary to answer the question"**.

541 @ 69 & 3 % 7 # 43 = ?
questions.solution:
The given equation is:

541 @ 69 & 3 % 7 # 43 = ?

Decoding the information, 

 
 

 
 
Symbol

 
 
 
#

 %

Meaning

×

The new equation is:

541 - 69 ÷ 3 × 7 + 43 = ?

 [IMAGE: https://lh5.googleusercontent.com/Ro308yDlMHZMoSnguV0wigWvPaVi44cD_wvabas7GQSDUI6EkfsS8WmcEjL6IMM8JHFvk9NUSyyPnObrQ7-yvuy4-15yELDTWsJUg68JE9ziEIXR4IjDG2Xd9k7OgV4KeTh8vfHj]

questions.question:
Select the option in which the numbers in the set share the same relationship as that shared by the numbers in the given set. (Note: Operations must be performed on whole numbers, without splitting the numbers into their component digits. Example 13 Operations on 13 such as addition/subtraction/multiplication etc. can be performed on 13. Breaking 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)

(21, 441, 9261)

(11,121, 1331)
questions.solution:
**Logic: **

**Second number = (First number)²**

**Third number = (First number)³**

(21, 441, 9261)→ 

(21)² = 441

(21)³ = 9261**

(11,121, 1331)→ 

(11)² = 121

(11)³ = 1331

Similarly,

**(1): (13, 169, 2197)**

(13)² = 169

(13)³ = 2197

Hence, the correct answer is “Option 1**”.
